posts.text:
In last revision I added new field &quot;config&quot; to &quot;slices&quot; table. Because this is very unpleasant to change database structure for every new configuration parameter for slices, I decided there is the best solution to have one database field which holds many config parameters. The configuration parameters are stored as XML - WDDX file, which is easy to maintain by PHP3. Parsing this field is done just on first access to slice - then the parameters are cached, so there is not slowdown of viewing.

For updating existing database you should use this two commands:

ALTER TABLE slices ADD config mediumtext

UPDATE slices set config=&quot;&lt;wddxPacket version='0.9'&gt;&lt;header/&gt;&lt;data&gt;&lt;struct&gt;&lt;var name='admin\_fields'&gt;&lt;struct&gt;&lt;var name='chbox'&gt;&lt;struct&gt;&lt;var name='width'&gt;&lt;number&gt;24&lt;/number&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;/struct&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;var name='post\_date'&gt;&lt;struct&gt;&lt;var name='width'&gt;&lt;number&gt;70&lt;/number&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;/struct&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;var name='headline'&gt;&lt;struct&gt;&lt;var name='width'&gt;&lt;number&gt;224&lt;/number&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;/struct&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;var name='catname'&gt;&lt;struct&gt;&lt;var name='width'&gt;&lt;number&gt;70&lt;/number&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;/struct&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;var name='published'&gt;&lt;struct&gt;&lt;var name='width'&gt;&lt;number&gt;24&lt;/number&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;/struct&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;var name='highlight'&gt;&lt;struct&gt;&lt;var name='width'&gt;&lt;number&gt;24&lt;/number&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;/struct&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;var name='feed'&gt;&lt;struct&gt;&lt;var name='width'&gt;&lt;number&gt;24&lt;/number&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;/struct&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;/struct&gt;&lt;/var&gt;&lt;/struct&gt;&lt;/data&gt;&lt;/wddxPacket&gt;&quot;

HonzaM

posts.text:
This is well known problem according to HTTP protocol. If you want to tell the browser to redirect to another page \(for example\), you can sent this command in HTTP header:

header\(&quot;Location: some-url.html&quot;\);

but the headers can be set only before any contents of page is send. After you send &lt;html&gt; ... or just a space, and then you will try to call heder function, the warning is displayed. 

If you can specify the page, where it appears, it will be great.

tickets.summary: Compact View page: Problems with Top HTML/Bottom HTML fields
tickets.description:
On the Compact view Customization page, there are two problems with the Bottom HTML and Top HTML fields:

1\. Form box too small:

The form box for these fields is only one line long. As a result, it is very hard to actually edit any text in these boxes.

2\. Field contents truncated

If you put anything long in these fields \(asy, one line or more\), then then the content of these fields is truncated next time you pull up the page. For example, I added

When I had made other changes to the form and resubmitted, the application assumed that I wanted &quot;&lt;br&gt;&lt;image src=&quot; to be the new value for the Top HTML field. The result was broken code.

There's a serious problem with feeding items that

called "file............"

set to:

http://\[domain\]/\[upload\_dir\]/\[Slice1\_ID\]/my\_file.pdf

\(which is fine\), but the value of Slice2's file............ 
field is set to:

http://\[domain\]/\[upload\_dir\]/\[Slice1\_ID\]/my\_file\_2.pdf

which is very, very bad because there is no

items that are fed from Slice1 the links to uploaded files 
are broken because the file names are wrong.

posts.subject: #93 New PHP 5.1 no longer offers HTTP_*_VARS
posts.author: russellmcormond

posts.text:
Logged In: YES 
user\_id=40086
Originator: NO

1\) If you set "register\_long\_arrays ON" in your php.ini file, then the HTTP\_\*\_VARS arrays are filled \(even if they are not listed in phpinfo\(\)\)

2\) I fixed the AA right now, so we no longer use HTTP\_\*\_VARS. AA should work with "register\_long\_arrays OFF" now. See SVN.

Honza
posts.subject: #93 New PHP 5.1 no longer offers HTTP_*_VARS
posts.author: honzam

posts.subject: #93 New PHP 5.1 no longer offers HTTP_*_VARS
posts.author: honzam

tickets.summary: New PHP 5.1 no longer offers HTTP_*_VARS
tickets.description:
We recently upgraded our server from RHEL3 to RHEL5 which includes php 5.1.6.  This version of php no longer offers the older long variables, and the "register\_long\_arrays" setting no longer does anything.

http://www.php.net/manual/en/ini.core.php\#ini.register-long-arrays

We could not log into AA until I changed some of the $HTTP\_GET\_VARS references to $\_GET .

I believe it is now time to do a global search-and-replace on:

s/$HTTP\_GET\_VARS/$\_GET/
s/$HTTP\_POST\_VARS/$\_POST/
s/$HTTP\_COOKIE\_VARS/$\_COOKIE/


I patched a few of the scripts, but not everything.  I'm awaiting advise from actual AA developers before proceeding given I have very little AA knowledge.
